_comment: Redacted, read-only baseline of the migration history production recorded, plus
the explicit mapping of differences an operator has reconciled against it.
STATUS: NOT CAPTURED. capture is null and rows is empty, which is what an
uncaptured baseline looks like. In this state the file accepts nothing and the
gate refuses on sight: supplying a reconciliation that records no capture is
itself a reported problem (reconciliation_without_capture), because production's
recorded history has never been read and nothing in the run compares it to
anything. Round-4 C4: before that check existed, this file's refusal was a
property of production happening to differ from the release, not of the gate —
an uncaptured baseline and an agreeing one reached the same outcome. That is the
intended state until an operator runs the capture, because production content
equivalence has not been demonstrated.
Fill it by running, from the release, against production:
node scripts/capture-remote-migration-history.mjs \
--url-file /etc/newme/migration-db.url \
--out supabase/migration-history-reconciliation.json
That is a read-only capture; it is still an authorised production action and is
not performed by any code round.
rows[] carries version, name, statement_count and a server-computed
statements_sha256 only. Never statement text, never business data, never an
identity. accepted[] entries must restate the observation they explain and are
re-matched against production on every run; an acceptance that matches nothing
is a refusal of its own. Rules and procedure:
supabase/preflight/migration-history-reconciliation.md
